tasks.title: Arrange Largest Number
tasks.instruction: Arrange the numbers from left to right to form the largest possible number, and place them on the pad.
tasks.scene: Four number tiles lie separately on the table, with four target pads arranged in a row.
tasks.procedure: Determine the descending numerical order that forms the largest possible number and place the tiles on the pads.
tasks.order: Place the tiles from left to right in descending numerical order.

subtasks.text: Place the largest number on the leftmost mat.
Place the largest number outside the mats on the second mat from the left.
Place the largest number outside the mats on the third mat from the left.
Place the remaining number on the fourth mat from the left.

counterfactual.original: Arrange the numbers from left to right to form the largest possible number, and place them on the pad.

changes.Actions: arrange to form largest number → turn face down and arrange left to right
changes.Placement: on pad → beside pad
changes.Constraints: largest → smallest

events.failure: The first, largest number is grasped incorrectly.
events.continuation: Place the wrong number on the first pad, then place the remaining three numbers in descending order.
events.effectiveRecovery: Return the wrongly grasped number and pick/place the correct largest number.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Return the wrongly grasped number, then pick/place a different incorrect number.

events.failure: The second-largest number is grasped incorrectly.
events.continuation: Place the wrong number on the second pad, then place the remaining two numbers in descending order.
events.effectiveRecovery: Return the wrongly grasped number and pick/place the correct second-largest number.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Return the wrongly grasped number, then pick/place a different incorrect number.

events.failure: The third-largest number is grasped incorrectly.
events.continuation: Place the wrong number on the third pad, then place the final number on the fourth pad.
events.effectiveRecovery: Return the wrongly grasped number and pick/place the correct third-largest number.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Return the wrongly grasped number, then pick/place a different incorrect number.

tasks.title: Fill Pen Holder
tasks.instruction: Pick up the pen holder, place all the pens into it one by one, then put the filled holder back on the table.
tasks.scene: An empty pen holder stands on the table, with four pens lying separately nearby.
tasks.procedure: Pick up the holder with one hand and use the other hand to insert all four pens individually, then return the filled holder to the table.
tasks.order: The pens may be inserted in any order. Picking up the holder precedes insertion, and putting it down follows all four insertions.

subtasks.text: Hold the empty pen holder.
Insert the first selected pen into the pen holder.
Insert the second selected pen into the pen holder.
Insert the third selected pen into the pen holder.
Insert the remaining pen into the pen holder.
Place the filled pen holder upright on the table.

counterfactual.original: Pick up the pen holder, place all the pens into it one by one, then put the filled holder back on the table.

changes.Actions: return holder to table → return holder to table upside down
changes.Placement: inside holder → beside holder
changes.Constraints: all pens → exactly three pens

events.failure: The pen holder is dropped while being grasped.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake placement of one pen at the holder and end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the holder again and complete the task.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick up the holder again but fail, then fake-place one pen and end.

events.failure: The second pen is dropped during grasp/transfer.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake insertion at the holder and end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the pen again and insert it successfully.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick up the pen again but fail, then fake-insert and end.

events.failure: The second pen is misaligned with the holder opening.
events.continuation: Continue the insertion motion outside the holder and end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Lift and realign the pen with the opening, then complete the task.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Lift the pen but move it farther from the opening, then continue the failed insertion and end.

events.failure: The fourth pen is dropped during grasp/transfer.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake insertion at the holder and end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the pen again and insert it successfully.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick up the pen again but fail, then fake-insert and end.

events.failure: The fourth pen is misaligned with the holder opening.
events.continuation: Continue the insertion motion outside the holder and end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Lift and realign the pen with the opening, then complete the task.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Lift the pen but move it farther from the opening, then continue the failed insertion and end.

multiSolutionTrajectories.description: The four pens may be inserted in any order after the holder is picked up; return the filled holder only after all four insertions. The task has 20 represented pen orders.

tasks.title: Fold Clothes
tasks.instruction: Fold the left sleeve inward toward the opposite chest point, fold the right sleeve inward toward the opposite chest point, then fold the lower hem upward until it is aligned with the shoulders.
tasks.scene: An unfolded garment lies flat on the table, with both sleeves extended.
tasks.procedure: Fold both sleeves across the body of the clothes, then fold the lower section upward over them.
tasks.order: Fold the left sleeve first, the right sleeve second, and the lower hem last.

subtasks.text: Fold the left sleeve inward.
Fold the right sleeve inward.
Fold the lower half of the garment over the upper half.

counterfactual.original: Fold the left sleeve inward toward the opposite chest point, fold the right sleeve inward toward the opposite chest point, then fold the lower hem upward until it is aligned with the shoulders.

changes.Actions: three folds → leave completely unfolded on table
changes.Placement: hem upward until aligned with shoulders → hem downward away from shoulders
changes.Constraints: both sleeves and hem folded → exactly one sleeve folded; rest unfolded

events.failure: The left sleeve is dropped because it is not grasped securely.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake folding motion.
events.effectiveRecovery: Regrasp the left sleeve and complete the task.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to regrasp the left sleeve but fail, then continue with a fake fold.

events.failure: The right sleeve is dropped because it is not grasped securely.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake folding motion.
events.effectiveRecovery: Regrasp the right sleeve and complete the task.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to regrasp the right sleeve but fail, then continue with a fake fold.

events.failure: The garment is dropped before it is folded in half.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake folding motion.
events.effectiveRecovery: Regrasp the garment and complete the fold.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to regrasp the garment but fail, then continue with a fake fold.

tasks.title: Hang Mugs
tasks.instruction: Hang all three mugs on the mug rack.
tasks.scene: Three mugs are placed separately on the table beside an empty mug rack.
tasks.procedure: Pick up and hang all three mugs on the rack, using an empty hook for each mug.
tasks.order: The mugs may be hung in any order.

subtasks.text: Hang the first cup on an empty hook.
Hang the second cup on another empty hook.
Hang the third cup on the remaining empty hook.

counterfactual.original: Hang all three mugs on the mug rack.

changes.Actions: hang on rack → stand upright on table
changes.Placement: hang on rack → place beside rack
changes.Constraints: all three → exactly two; one on table

events.failure: The first mug handle is not aligned with the rack and the mug is released.
events.continuation: Release the misaligned mug so it falls, then end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick the mug up again, align its handle, and hang it.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick the mug up again but fail, then continue with a fake placement and end.

events.failure: The second mug handle is not aligned with the rack and the mug is released.
events.continuation: Release the misaligned mug so it falls, then end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick the mug up again, align its handle, and hang it.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick the mug up again but fail, then continue with a fake placement and end.

events.failure: The third mug handle is not aligned with the rack and the mug is released.
events.continuation: Release the misaligned mug so it falls, then end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick the mug up again, align its handle, and hang it.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick the mug up again but fail, then continue with a fake placement and end.

multiSolutionTrajectories.description: The three mugs may be hung in different orders, with different assignments of mugs to the left and right arms. The page presents 20 valid variations.

tasks.title: Insert Tubes
tasks.instruction: Insert the three tubes into the rack one by one.
tasks.scene: Three tubes lie separately on the table in front of an empty tube rack.
tasks.procedure: Pick up and insert each tube into an empty rack slot until all three tubes are in the rack.
tasks.order: Insert the tubes one by one in any order.

subtasks.text: Insert the first tube into an empty slot.
Insert the second tube into another empty slot.
Insert the third tube into the remaining empty slot.

counterfactual.original: Insert three tubes into the rack one by one.

changes.Actions: insert → rotate each tube once, then insert
changes.Placement: insert into rack → place beside rack
changes.Constraints: three → exactly two; one on table

events.failure: The second tube is dropped during grasp/transfer.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake placement at the tube-rack slot and end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick the tube up again and complete the insertion sequence.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick the tube up again but fail, then fake-place and end.

events.failure: The third tube is dropped during grasp/transfer.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake placement at the tube-rack slot and end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick the tube up again and complete the insertion sequence.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick the tube up again but fail, then fake-place and end.

events.failure: The second tube misses its rack slot because it is misaligned.
events.continuation: Ignore the failed insertion and continue with the remaining actions.
events.effectiveRecovery: Lift and realign the tube, then insert it successfully.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Lift and attempt to realign the tube but leave it outside the slot, then continue.

events.failure: The third tube misses its rack slot because it is misaligned.
events.continuation: Ignore the failed insertion and continue with the remaining actions.
events.effectiveRecovery: Lift and realign the tube, then insert it successfully.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Lift and attempt to realign the tube but leave it outside the slot, then continue.

tasks.title: Make Toast
tasks.instruction: Pick up two bread slices one by one, place them into the toaster, and press the lever down.
tasks.scene: Bread slices are placed beside a toaster with two empty slots on the table.
tasks.procedure: Pick up two slices one by one, insert them into the toaster’s two slots, and press the lever down.
tasks.order: Both slices must be inserted before the lever is pressed.

subtasks.text: Insert the first bread slice into one toaster slot.
Insert the second bread slice into the remaining toaster slot.
Press the toaster lever down.

counterfactual.original: Pick up two bread slices one by one, place them into the toaster, and press the lever down.

changes.Actions: press lever down → leave lever up
changes.Placement: into toaster → beside toaster
changes.Constraints: two slices → exactly one

events.failure: The first bread slice is dropped before entering the toaster.
events.continuation: Continue with a placement motion as though the slice were in the slot.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the slice and insert it before continuing.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick up the slice but fail, then perform the nominal placement motion.

events.failure: The second slice is misaligned at the toaster slot.
events.continuation: Move on to the next subtask without correcting the slice.
events.effectiveRecovery: Realign and insert the slice, then continue.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Attempt realignment but leave it misaligned, then proceed.

events.failure: The control is pressed off target.
events.continuation: Continue the downward motion without contacting the control.
events.effectiveRecovery: Reposition over the control and press it.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Reposition incorrectly and miss the control again.

tasks.title: Organize Table
tasks.instruction: Place the alarm clock on the drawer, put the figurine on its stand, place the mouse on the mouse pad, and push the keyboard into the frame.
tasks.scene: An alarm clock, a figurine, a mouse, and a keyboard are placed on the table, outside their respective destinations: a drawer top, a figurine stand, a mouse pad, and a keyboard frame.
tasks.procedure: Place the alarm clock on the drawer top, the figurine on its stand, and the mouse on its pad, and push the keyboard into its frame.
tasks.order: The four placements have no required global order.

subtasks.text: Place the alarm clock on top of the drawer.
Place the figurine on the stand.
Place the mouse on the mouse pad.
Insert the keyboard into the frame.

counterfactual.original: Place the alarm clock on the drawer, put the figurine on its stand, place the mouse on the mouse pad, and push the keyboard into the frame.

changes.Objects: figurine on its stand; mouse on mouse pad → figurine on mouse pad; mouse on stand
changes.Actions: push keyboard into frame → leave keyboard outside frame
changes.Placement: mouse on pad → beside pad
changes.Constraints: all four → exactly one; three stay initial

events.failure: The alarm clock is dropped because it is not grasped securely.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake placement on the cabinet.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick the alarm clock up again and complete the task.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick it up again but fail, then continue with a fake placement and end.

events.failure: The figure is dropped because it is not grasped securely.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake placement in front of the screen.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick the figure up again and complete the task.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick it up again but fail, then continue with a fake placement.

events.failure: The mouse is dropped because it is not grasped securely.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake placement on the black mat.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick the mouse up again and complete the task.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick it up again but fail, then continue with a fake placement and end.

events.failure: The keyboard is pushed clearly in the wrong direction.
events.continuation: Continue the incorrect push and end in failure.
events.effectiveRecovery: Push it again in the correct direction and complete the placement.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Attempt to correct the push direction, but leave the keyboard misplaced.

tasks.title: Press By Number
tasks.instruction: Press the two red buttons the required number of times according to the number cards, then press the blue button to confirm.
tasks.scene: Two number cards lie above two corresponding red buttons on the table, with a blue confirmation button beside them.
tasks.procedure: Read the two cards and press each red button the corresponding number of times, then press the blue button to confirm.
tasks.order: The required press counts vary with the cards. Complete the red-button presses before pressing the blue confirmation button.

subtasks.text: Press the first button the required number of times.
Press the blue button.
Press the second button the required number of times.
Press the blue button again.

tasks.title: Put Bottles Into Dustbin
tasks.instruction: Pick up all four bottles one by one and throw them into the dustbin.
tasks.scene: Four bottles are placed on the table, with a dustbin beside the table.
tasks.procedure: Pick up and deposit all four bottles in the dustbin.
tasks.order: Handle the bottles one by one, order is not specified.

subtasks.text: Place the first bottle in the dustbin.
Place the second bottle in the dustbin.
Place the third bottle in the dustbin.
Place the last bottle in the dustbin.

counterfactual.original: Pick up all four bottles one by one and throw them into the dustbin.

changes.Actions: throw into bin → stand upright on table
changes.Placement: throw into dustbin → place beside dustbin
changes.Constraints: all four → exactly three; one on table

events.failure: A bottle is dropped during the initial grasp.
events.continuation: Continue with a nominal transfer/dump motion although the bottle was not secured.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the bottle, stabilize it, and place it in the bin.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry the grasp unsuccessfully, then continue/end without a valid deposit.

events.failure: The bottle is dropped during the handoff between grippers.
events.continuation: Continue the receiving-arm motion as if the handoff succeeded.
events.effectiveRecovery: Adjust the receiving pose/grip, complete the handoff, and deposit the bottle.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Attempt an incorrect handoff adjustment, drop the bottle again, then continue with a nominal dump.

events.failure: The bottle is dropped while being carried toward the bin.
events.continuation: Continue or return with the failed carry without making a valid deposit.
events.effectiveRecovery: Regrasp the bottle and place it in the bin.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry the grasp but drop it again, then end the attempt.

tasks.title: Pack Objects Into Box
tasks.instruction: Move the box to the center of the table, then place all the objects into the box.
tasks.scene: An open box and four separate objects are placed on the table, with the objects initially outside the box.
tasks.procedure: Clear the center of the table and move the box there, then pick up and place all four objects inside.
tasks.order: The objects may be packed in any order after the box is positioned.

subtasks.text: Clear the center of the table, then place the box in the center of the table.
Place the shoe into the box.
Place the hammer into the box.
Place the toothbrush into the box.
Place the toy car into the box.

counterfactual.original: Move the box to the center of the table, then place all the objects into the box.

changes.Actions: place objects in box → place in box, then remove to table
changes.Placement: inside box → beside box
changes.Constraints: all objects → exactly three; one outside

events.failure: The box is dropped because it is not grasped securely.
events.continuation: Continue with a fake placement of the box in front; fake-place the later objects there as well.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick the box up again and complete the task.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick the box up again but fail, then continue fake-placing the later objects in front.

events.failure: The shoe is dropped during grasp/transfer.
events.continuation: Do not recover it; continue to the next item.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the shoe and place it in the box.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick it up again but fail, then continue with a fake placement and end.

events.failure: The hammer is dropped during grasp/transfer.
events.continuation: Do not recover it; continue to the next item.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the hammer and place it in the box.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick it up again but fail, then continue with a fake placement and end.

events.failure: The toothbrush is dropped during grasp/transfer.
events.continuation: Do not recover it; continue to the next item.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the toothbrush and place it in the box.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick it up again but fail, then continue with a fake placement and end.

events.failure: The toy car is dropped during grasp/transfer.
events.continuation: Do not recover it; continue to the next item/end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the toy car and place it in the box.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick it up again but fail, then continue with a fake placement and end.

multiSolutionTrajectories.description: After the box is positioned, the four objects may be packed in different orders, with different assignments of objects to the two arms. The page presents 20 valid variations.

tasks.title: Play Stacking Toy
tasks.instruction: Place the four matching pieces onto the longest peg one by one, place the three matching pieces onto the second-longest peg, place the two matching pieces onto the second-shortest peg, then place the remaining piece onto the shortest peg.
tasks.scene: A stacking-toy base with four pegs of different lengths lies on the table. Ten matching pieces lie separately around it, with four, three, two, and one piece for the respective pegs.
tasks.procedure: Load the longest peg with its four matching pieces, the second-longest with three, the second-shortest with two, and the shortest with the remaining piece.
tasks.order: Follow the peg order from longest to shortest and place the pieces individually.

subtasks.text: Place the four matching pieces on the longest peg.
Place the three matching pieces on the secondlongest peg.
Place the two matching pieces on the secondshortest peg.
Place the remaining piece on the shortest peg.

counterfactual.original: Place the four matching pieces onto the longest peg one by one, place the three matching pieces onto the second-longest peg, place the two matching pieces onto the second-shortest peg, then place the remaining piece onto the shortest peg.

changes.Actions: place on pegs → rotate in place; leave on table
changes.Placement: longest to shortest pegs → shortest to longest pegs
changes.Constraints: per-peg counts 4/3/2/1 → per-peg counts 3/2/1/0; four remain on table

events.failure: A piece is dropped while placing a group of pieces.
events.continuation: Continue the sequence with a nominal placement on the corresponding peg.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the piece and place it on its assigned peg.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry the grasp unsuccessfully, then perform the nominal placement motion.

events.failure: A piece is assigned to the wrong peg.
events.continuation: Leave it on the wrong peg and continue with the remaining pieces.
events.effectiveRecovery: Move it from the wrong peg to its assigned peg.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Attempt to move it but leave it on the wrong peg.

events.failure: A peg and hole are misaligned, so the piece misses or tilts beside the base.
events.continuation: Continue to the next step without seating the piece.
events.effectiveRecovery: Realign the piece and insert it into the hole.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry alignment but leave the piece tilted or unseated.

events.failure: A single piece is not fully seated after pressing.
events.continuation: Continue the pressing motion without achieving insertion.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up/re-align the piece and press it fully into place.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry with an incorrect alignment, leaving it unseated.

tasks.title: Stack Blocks
tasks.instruction: Stack the three blocks with different textures into one stable pile.
tasks.scene: Three blocks with different textures are placed separately on the table.
tasks.procedure: Place a base block at the table center, stack a second block on it, and place the third on top to form one stable pile.
tasks.order: The blocks may be selected in any order. Each supporting block must be in place before the next block is stacked on it.

subtasks.text: Place the first block in the center of the table.
Place the second block on the first block.
Place the third block on the second block.

counterfactual.original: Stack the three blocks with different textures into one stable pile.

changes.Actions: stack in pile → rotate in place; no stack
changes.Placement: stack in one pile → arrange side by side on table
changes.Constraints: one 3-block pile → one 2-block stack + one single block

events.failure: The first block is dropped.
events.continuation: Continue with a nominal placement motion although the block is not placed.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the block and complete the stack.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry the grasp unsuccessfully, then continue the nominal placement motion.

events.failure: The second block overlaps the first by less than 40%.
events.continuation: Leave the unstable placement; placing the next block causes the stack to collapse.
events.effectiveRecovery: Reposition the second block to a stable overlap, then continue.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Make a small push/side adjustment that leaves overlap below 40%, then continue into collapse.

events.failure: The third block overlaps by less than 20%.
events.continuation: Continue, allowing the top block to collapse.
events.effectiveRecovery: Reposition it to a stable overlap.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Attempt an adjustment but leave the overlap insufficient, so the top block collapses.

multiSolutionTrajectories.description: The three blocks may be selected in different orders and assigned to different arms, while placement must respect support: each lower block must be in place before the block above it. The page presents 20 valid variations.

tasks.title: Store Laptop And Headphones
tasks.instruction: Hang the headphones on the headphone stand, close the laptop, then place the closed laptop into the vertical laptop stand.
tasks.scene: An open laptop rests on a laptop stand. Headphones, an empty headphone stand, and an empty vertical laptop stand are placed nearby.
tasks.procedure: Hang the headphones on their stand, close the laptop, lift it from its initial stand, and insert it into the vertical laptop stand.
tasks.order: Hang the headphones first, close the laptop second, and place the closed laptop in the vertical stand last.

subtasks.text: Place the headphones on the headphone stand.
Close the laptop.
Place the closed laptop in the laptop stand.

counterfactual.original: Hang the headphones on the headphone stand, close the laptop, then place the closed laptop into the vertical laptop stand.

changes.Actions: close laptop → leave open
changes.Placement: into laptop stand → beside laptop stand
changes.Constraints: headphones/laptop on their own stands → both on headphone stand; laptop stand empty

events.failure: The headphones are misaligned and fall during hanging.
events.continuation: Continue to the laptop subtask without rehanging them.
events.effectiveRecovery: Regrasp, adjust the angle, and hang the headphones securely.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry hanging with an incorrect pose so they fall again.

events.failure: The laptop remains open because it is offset.
events.continuation: Continue with a nominal insertion into the storage slot.
events.effectiveRecovery: Adjust the laptop until it closes, then store it.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Attempt to close it but leave it open, then perform the nominal insertion.

events.failure: The laptop is misaligned during insertion.
events.continuation: Continue/return from the slot without correcting the alignment.
events.effectiveRecovery: Realign and insert the laptop.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry insertion but leave it misaligned.

tasks.title: Swap Blocks
tasks.instruction: Swap the two blocks using the empty mat, pressing the button after each move.
tasks.scene: Three mats are arranged in a row on the table. Two hold one block each, the third is empty, and a button lies nearby.
tasks.procedure: Move one block to the empty mat, move the other block to the newly vacant mat, and move the first block to the second block’s original mat, so that the two blocks exchange positions.
tasks.order: Press the button after every block move.

subtasks.text: Put the first block on the empty mat.
Press the button to confirm the first move.
Transfer the second block onto the original first block’s position.
Press the button to confirm the second move.
Put the first block on the original second block’s mat.
Press the button to confirm the last move.

tasks.title: Sweep Blocks
tasks.instruction: Pick up the broom, pick up and place the dustpan upright on the table, then use the broom to sweep all the objects into the dustpan.
tasks.scene: A broom and an empty dustpan lie on the table beside several scattered blocks.
tasks.procedure: Pick up the broom, pick up and position the dustpan upright on the table, and sweep all blocks into it.
tasks.order: Pick up the broom first and position the dustpan before sweeping.

subtasks.text: Pick up the broom.
Pick up the dustpan.
Sweep all objects into the dustpan.

counterfactual.original: Pick up the broom, pick up and place the dustpan upright on the table, then use the broom to sweep all the objects into the dustpan.

changes.Actions: sweep into dustpan → scatter away from dustpan
changes.Placement: into dustpan → beside dustpan
changes.Constraints: sweep all objects into dustpan → sweep exactly one object into dustpan

events.failure: The broom is dropped during the handoff.
events.continuation: Continue with nominal sweeping motions without securing the broom.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the broom and stabilize the handoff, then sweep.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry the pickup/grip unsuccessfully and continue.

events.failure: The dustpan is placed with an incorrect orientation (about 90° off).
events.continuation: Sweep with the dustpan misoriented; no blocks are collected.
events.effectiveRecovery: Rotate it to the correct orientation and sweep.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Make only a small 15–30° correction, leaving it misoriented; no blocks are collected.

events.failure: The sweep misses part of the blocks.
events.continuation: Sweep only part of the set and stop without checking/completing the remainder.
events.effectiveRecovery: Sweep the remaining blocks into the dustpan.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Make another incomplete sweep, leaving blocks outside the dustpan.

tasks.title: Apply Dish Soap Repeatedly
tasks.instruction: Press the dish-soap bottle 5 times continuously, dispensing soap onto the dishcloth.
tasks.scene: A dish-soap dispenser sits at the table center, with a dishcloth lying to its right.
tasks.procedure: Hold the cloth beneath the outlet with the right arm while the left arm presses and releases the pump, then return the cloth to the dispenser’s right.

subtasks.text: Place the dishcloth below the pump outlet.
Press the pump for the first time.
Press the pump for the second time.
Press the pump for the third time.
Press the pump for the fourth time.
Press the pump for the fifth time.
Place the dishcloth on the table.

tasks.title: Arrange Family Tea Set
tasks.instruction: Place the teacup on the cat-head mat, the teapot on the yellow mat, the lid on the teapot, the tongs in their holder, and the canister on the round mat. Complete these placements in any order, provided the teapot is placed before its lid.
tasks.scene: A cup, a teapot, and a tea canister sit off their designated coasters on the table. The teapot lid lies beside the teapot, and tea tongs lie outside their holder.
tasks.procedure: Place the cup on the left-front coaster, the teapot on the right-front teapot coaster, the lid on the teapot, the tea canister on the teacanister coaster, and the tea tongs in the bamboo holder tool position.

subtasks.text: Place the cup on the left-front coaster.
Place the teapot on the right-front teapot coaster.
Place the lid on the teapot.
Place the tea canister on the tea-canister coaster.
Place the tea tongs in the bamboo holder.

counterfactual.original: Place the teacup on the cat-head mat, the teapot on the yellow mat, the lid on the teapot, the tongs in their holder, and the canister on the round mat. Complete these placements in any order, provided the teapot is placed before its lid.

changes.Objects: teacup on cat-head mat; teapot on yellow mat → teacup on yellow mat; teapot on cat-head mat
changes.Actions: lid on teapot → leave lid off teapot

Place the plate face up in the lower center of the placemat and the bowl open side up in the upper center, in front of the plate. Place the fork on the left and the knife on the right, with the fork tines and knife tip pointing toward the front. Complete these actions in any order.

events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to adjust the fork but leave it on the right, then place the knife on the left.

events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to rotate/reposition it but leave it reversed, then end.

events.failure: FRT-5: the knife is released outside the tablecloth.
events.continuation: Leave it outside the tablecloth and end.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick it up, orient it forward, and place it in the right target zone.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to reposition it but release it outside the tablecloth again, then end.

tasks.instruction: Place the red block on the yellow drawer, the yellow block on the white drawer, and the blue block on the dark-green drawer, in that order.
tasks.scene: Three drawer storage units are arranged in a row across the table. Red, yellow, and blue blocks form a separate row in front of them.
tasks.procedure: Place the red, yellow, and blue blocks on top of the yellow, white, and dark-green storage units, respectively.

subtasks.text: Place the red block on the yellow drawer.
Place the yellow block on the white drawer.
Place the blue block on the dark-green drawer.

counterfactual.original: Place the red block on the yellow drawer, the yellow block on the white drawer, and the blue block on the dark-green drawer, in that order.

events.failure: FRT-1: the red block is placed on the middle white slot before the yellow block is placed on the left slot.

events.ineffectiveRecovery: Try to pick up the blue block but drop it in the same recovery zone again, then perform the nominal empty placement and end.

tasks.instruction: Place the three colored blocks on the plate one at a time in the order red, green, then blue. Tilt the loaded plate to pour all three blocks into the box.

events.failure: The plate/bowl is not grasped.
events.continuation: End or continue the nominal transfer without a secured plate.
events.effectiveRecovery: Grasp the plate and continue the transfer.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry with another empty grasp, then end/continue without it.

events.failure: The first block is released outside the plate.
events.continuation: Leave it outside and continue transferring the remaining blocks/tilting the plate.
events.effectiveRecovery: Pick up the block, put it on the plate, and continue.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Attempt to pick/place it but leave it outside, then continue.

events.failure: The grasp of the second block is empty.
events.continuation: Continue with a nominal placement motion and end the attempt.
events.effectiveRecovery: Regrasp the block and continue the transfer.
events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry unsuccessfully, then perform the nominal placement motion.

events.failure: The plate with blocks is dropped during transport.
events.continuation: Continue with a nominal dump motion although the plate was not carried successfully.

events.ineffectiveRecovery: Retry the grasp unsuccessfully, then perform the nominal dump motion.
